information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

IS: 8344 -1977 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SNARE, AURAL, GLEGG'S PATTERN 



( Reaffirmed 2006 ) 



1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for Glegg's pattern aural snare used in ENT 
surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions— As shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 1 SNARE, AURAL, GLEGG'S PATTERN 

2.1 A deviation of =fc 2"5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Materials 

3.1 Body — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 20Cr13 or 30Cr13 of IS : 6603-1972 ' Specifica- 
tion for stainless steel bars and flats' or brass conforming to Designation CuZn42Pb2 of 
IS : 3488-1966 ' Specification for brass bars rods and sections suitable for forging '. 

3.2 Wire — Hard drawn stainless steel wire conforming to Designation 07Cr18Ni9 or 04Cr18Ni10 of 
IS : 6528-1972 ' Specification for stainless steel wire '. 

3.3 The plunger shall be made of stainless steel conforming to Designation 20Cr13 or 30Cr13 of 
IS: 6603-1972. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The snare shall be finished smooth and free from burrs, pits, cracks and other surface defects. 

4.2 The loop of the thumb shall be removable so that the sliding component may be withdrawn to 
replace the wire. 

4.3 The sliding shall be smooth and free from jerk.

INDIAN STANDARDS INSTITUTION

IS: 8344 -1977 

4.4 The finger loops shall be smooth and properly rounded. 

4-5 The wire shall be of uniform diameter and shall be free from kinks, rust and other surface 
defects. 

4.6 The snare if made of stainless steel shall be polished bright and passivated. 

4.7 The brazzing or silver soldering shall be neat and sound. 

4.8 The brass component shall be plated chromium over nickel conforming to Grade 2 of IS : 4827- 
1968 ' Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on copper and copper alloys. 

5. Heat Treatment — The snare if made of stainless steel shall be uniformly hardened and temper- 
ed to give a hardness of 410 to 470 HV. 

6. Test 

6.1 Corrosion Resistance — The snare if made of stainless steel shall satisfy the boiling and 
autoclaving test conforming to IS : 7531-1975 ' Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion 
resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments 1 . 

7. Marking — The snare shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, 
initials, recognized trade-mark and the words" Stainless Steel " if made of stainless steel and the 
country of origin. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The wire for the snare shall be coated with a thin film of non-corrosive mineral oil. 
The snare shall be wrapped in moisture proof paper and packed individually in card-board cartons. 
The snare may be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



Printed at Neelkamal Printers. Delhi, Indto
